issues: CRITICAL: build_ruby_install_argv() (ruby_runtime.py:56) does not check if bundler is on PATH — returns ['bundle', ...] even when `shutil.which('bundle')` would return None. Caller will get FileNotFoundError. Compare with install_argv() which correctly guards on bundler().
CRITICAL: build_ruby_test_argv() (ruby_runtime.py:101) same bug — no PATH check for bundler before returning ['bundle', 'exec', ...]. Will crash at runtime if bundle is missing.

CRITICAL: test_argv() (ruby_runtime.py:81) accepts junit_xml_path parameter but never uses it — JUnit test report paths are silently discarded. Compare with python_runtime.py:111 which passes --junit-xml={junit_xml_path}. The verify subsystem expects structured test output at this path and will get nothing.

BUG: _SKIP in ruby_manifests.py:13 is {'.git', 'vendor', 'node_modules', '.bundle'} but ruby_runtime.py installs gems to '.depfix-bundle' (BUNDLE_PATH). _iter_gemfiles will traverse .depfix-bundle/ and could match gemspecs inside installed gems, attempting to rewrite third-party code. Must add '.depfix-bundle' to _SKIP.
BUG: ruby_lockfile_paths() (ruby_lockfile.py:12) filters 'vendor' and '.bundle' but not '.depfix-bundle' — same issue. Could find Gemfile.lock inside the gem install cache.

DESIGN: _iter_gemfiles iterates *.gemspec files but _GEM_LINE_RE only matches Gemfile `gem 'name'` syntax, not gemspec `spec.add_dependency 'name'` syntax. Gemspec files are found but never rewritten — silent no-op that gives false confidence. Either add gemspec regex support or remove *.gemspec from the glob.

DESIGN: Duplicate function pairs with inconsistent behavior: install_argv() vs build_ruby_install_argv() (different retry/frozen/PATH-check semantics), test_argv() vs build_ruby_test_argv() (different detection heuristics for minitest). One pair should be canonical; the other should be removed or made a wrapper.

COVERAGE: Zero dedicated unit tests for ruby_runtime.py, ruby_manifests.py, ruby_lockfile.py, and ruby_validator.py. The only ruby tests are in test_ecosystems_manifests.py testing scan_ruby_dependencies (a different module). Every bug listed above would have been caught by basic unit tests.
